rules.title: Add tests with changes
rules.text: Add or update tests for every behavior change and bug fix.

rules.title: Reproduce bugs first
rules.text: For bug fixes, write a failing test that reproduces the bug before fixing it.

rules.title: Test pyramid
rules.text: Prefer many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and a small number of end-to-end tests.

rules.title: Mock only boundaries
rules.text: Mock only external boundaries (network, clock, filesystem); use real collaborators otherwise.

rules.title: Deterministic tests
rules.text: Keep tests deterministic: no real time, randomness or network without control.

rules.title: Test-driven development
rules.text: Work test-first: write a failing test, make it pass, then refactor.

rules.title: Coverage threshold
rules.text: Do not lower the coverage threshold; new code should be covered.

rules.title: Independent tests
rules.text: Keep tests independent; no shared mutable state or required execution order.

rules.title: Arrange, act, assert
rules.text: Structure tests as arrange, act, assert with one behavior per test.

rules.title: Factories over shared fixtures
rules.text: Build test data with small factories instead of large shared fixtures.

rules.title: No flaky tests
rules.text: Treat a flaky test as a bug: find the cause instead of adding retries or sleeps.

rules.title: Contract tests
rules.text: Cover service boundaries with contract tests so consumers and providers cannot drift.

rules.title: Snapshots sparingly
rules.text: Use snapshot tests only for small stable outputs and review snapshot diffs carefully.

rules.title: Property-based tests
rules.text: Use property-based tests for parsers, serializers and invariants.

rules.title: Test public behavior
rules.text: Test public behavior rather than private functions or implementation details.

rules.title: Performance regression checks
rules.text: Add benchmarks for performance-critical paths and compare against a baseline.

rules.title: Meaningful assertions
rules.text: Make assertions specific enough that the test fails if the behavior breaks.
